title: Dynamic ARP Inspection and Spoofing Defense
summary: Configure and verify Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) on Cisco Catalyst switches, establish trusted and untrusted port boundaries, configure ARP inspection rate limiting, activate multi-attribute validation checks (src-mac, dst-mac, ip), integrate with DHCP snooping bindings, and observe Layer 2 ARP security behavior.
learning_objectives: Explain the mechanics of Gratuitous ARP poisoning and ARP cache spoofing attacks in broadcast domains
Configure DHCP Snooping as a foundational prerequisite to populate the secure Layer 2 IP-to-MAC binding database
Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) globally for active access VLANs
Designate trusted interfaces for default gateways and network uplinks while maintaining untrusted boundaries on host ports
Implement ARP packet rate limiting on untrusted access interfaces to protect the switch CPU against denial-of-service floods
Configure advanced ARP validation rules verifying Source MAC, Destination MAC, and IP address consistency
Verify DAI operational status, interface trust states, binding integration, and end-to-end legitimate host communication

source.origin: Independently authored network security laboratory guide based on RFC 826 (Ethernet Address Resolution Protocol) and Cisco IOS Dynamic ARP Inspection security architecture
